title: Buying EURC (EURC): Safest Exchanges and Steps
content:
EURC is an essential tool for those looking to maintain exposure to the euro while navigating the blockchain ecosystem. By providing a transparent, regulated, and fiat-backed stablecoin, Circle has created a bridge similar to the role [USDC](/usd-coin) plays for the dollar.

## Why Buy EURC? EURC allows users to hedge against USD volatility or settle trades directly in euros on-chain. It is particularly useful for

European traders looking to minimize conversion friction when interacting with DeFi protocols or platforms that support euro-denominated pairs.

## Market Availability Checks for EURC

Before depositing funds, verify current EURC market availability directly in the exchange or DEX interface. Listings, liquidity, regional access, and withdrawal networks change over time, so treat venue availability as something to confirm at the point of purchase.

Use this checklist before placing an order:
- Search for the exact EURC ticker and EURC name.
- Confirm the trading pair, contract address, and network.
- Compare spread, volume, withdrawal fees, and minimum order size.
- Send a small test withdrawal before moving a larger balance.

## Purchase Tutorial 1.

Sign up for a reputable exchange that supports EURC. 2. Complete the necessary KYC (Know Your Customer) identity verification. 3. Deposit fiat currency (EUR) into your exchange account. 4. Navigate to the trading section and locate the EURC/EUR or EURC/[USDC](/usd-coin) trading pair. 5. Execute your order according to your personal financial strategy. 6. Withdraw your tokens to a private wallet for long-term storage.

## Securing Your Tokens

Storing assets on an exchange carries inherent risks. For long-term holdings, use a non-custodial hardware wallet. These devices keep your private keys offline, protecting you from exchange-level vulnerabilities. Always double-check the contract address before sending funds.

## Important Risks As noted in our TokenRadar analysis, EURC has a Risk Score of 5.

While it is stable, all on-chain assets carry technical risks, including potential smart contract vulnerabilities. Ensure you are aware of the network fees associated with your chosen chain, such as [Ethereum](/ethereum) or [Avalanche](/avalanche-2), before initiating transactions.
